title: Referenced files and the file-access modes
summary: Which files a document may reference, the --file-access and --allow-root options, the diagnostics of a denial, and the Pandoc filter.

items.text: The default. A document may reference every regular local file, as Pandoc reads them: a path relative to the file that holds the link, a path with .., an absolute or drive path, a local file: URI, and a symbolic link or junction.

Only a file inside a folder named by --allow-root, or, without --allow-root, inside the current folder or the folder of an input. Both the path as written and the real path of the opened file must be inside, so a link that leads out is denied, and so is a path outside that links back in.
A reference may not pass through a symbolic link or junction below the folder of the input it starts from; that folder and the folders above it are trusted. A hard link cannot be detected.
Both rules: the folder confinement that earlier versions applied by default. --file-access roots,no-symlinks restores it, and --allow-root names other folders.

Chooses the mode for render and its verbs, inspect, compare, montage, and flatten: any, roots, no-symlinks, or roots,no-symlinks, in any letter case. Anything else is a usage-error that lists the modes. info always measures under any.

A folder that referenced files may be in; repeatable. It implies --file-access roots and replaces the default folders. A relative folder is taken from the current folder, and a folder that does not exist is a usage-error. With --file-access any or no-symlinks it is a usage-error that names the conflict.
The files named on the command line are never judged by the mode, only the files they reference: images, pictures, data files, includes, and linked pages, at every level.
A network URL (http:, https:, and other schemes), a UNC or network path, a file: URI with a host, a device path, an alternate data stream, and anything that is not a regular file are never read.
Every size and count limit holds in every mode; a mode decides which files may be read, never how much. See 'canvasnet help limits'.

Warning: a picture (an SVG image, a Mermaid picture, a Vega-Lite image mark, or a linked page) that the mode denies is not drawn, and the rest is; the message names the link, the mode, and why. With --strict it is the error file-access-denied.

Error: an OpenSCAD include or use file or a Vega-Lite data file that the mode denies, or a denied picture with --strict; the message names the file as written and where it is referenced. No output is written.
A mode other than any needs the real path of every opened file. Where the system cannot tell it (Linux without /proc, for example), the file is denied, never read unchecked.

In the JSON result, the detail of an image-access-denied note holds the reference, the requested and real paths, and the mode. These are host paths: a service that shows notes to untrusted authors should remove them.
docs/filters/canvasnet.lua passes no mode, so a document reads its pictures, includes, and data as Pandoc reads its images.
Set it to roots, no-symlinks, or roots,no-symlinks to pass --file-access to every render and flatten of the filter; a picture the mode denies then stops the build.

Folders separated like PATH (; on Windows, : elsewhere), passed as one --allow-root each; it implies roots. Both variables are part of the cache name of every picture, so a picture drawn without them is not reused with them.

examples.name: confine
examples.description: Render a drawing whose links must stay in the docs and assets folders.
examples.content: canvasnet render docs/diagram.svg --allow-root docs --allow-root assets -o diagram.png --json

examples.name: no-links
examples.description: The folder confinement of earlier versions: the current folder and the folder of the input, and no symbolic links.

examples.name: strict
examples.description: Fail instead of leaving out a picture the mode denies.
